newsitem.title: UK: Cadbury shares extend gains after results.
newsitem.headline: Cadbury shares extend gains after results.

text.p: Cadbury Schweppes Plc shares rose on Thursday on positive analyst comment after Wednesday's results and the company's promise of greater focus on shareholder value, traders and analysts said.
Extending Wednesday's 19p rise, the stock was up 15-1/2p at 544-1/2 by 0906 GMT after earlier hitting a year's high of 545p.
"It is literally just a follow-through from the results yesterday with some positive comment," said one market-maker in the stock.

Analyst Richard Newboult at Lehman Brothers repeated a "buy" on Cadbury shares, noting that underlying growth of between 11 and 12 percent and a stronger commitment to realising shareholder value suggested that a prospective price-earnings multiple of 13.7 times was too low.

"We believe that Cadbury has passed an important milestone in terms of its understanding of shareholder concerns," Newboult said in a research note, "and this manifested itself in an unusually confident and powerful presentation by new chief executive John Sunderland."
He also highlighted Cadbury's proposal to link executive pay with total shareholder return and said he had raised his estimate for 1997 pre-tax profit to 598 million stg from 590 million.

Separately the Financial Times said Cadbury was ready to spend up to 1 billion stg on acquisitions following last months's 623 million stg sale of its 51 percent stake in bottling operation Coca-Cola Schweppes Beverages.
However not all were convinced of the strength of the company's new strategy and acquisition plans.
"It just means they will be spending more money," said one dealer, "I don't really know why the shares have been so strong."
Yesterday's results showed a 16 percent rise in pre-tax profit to 592 million stg, at the top of the range of analyst expectations.
